BearSSL, vendored into hawkOS
=============================

Upstream:  https://www.bearssl.org/git/BearSSL
Commit:    7bea48e5e850ab4cafbe68d3765cdaba13a86d6f  (2026-04-06)
Licence:   MIT — see LICENSE.txt in this directory
Author:    Thomas Pornin

The tree is committed as plain files rather than as a submodule, so that
cloning hawkOS is enough to build it. The upstream .git directory was
removed for the same reason; the commit hash above is what to check out if
you want to diff against upstream or update.

NOTHING IN THIS DIRECTORY IS MODIFIED. Everything hawkOS needs in order to
use BearSSL lives outside it:

  tools/build_bearssl.sh   compiles src/ for the kernel's freestanding
                           i386 target and archives it as
                           build/libbearssl.a. It excludes src/rand/sysrng.c
                           (which wants /dev/urandom or the Windows crypto
                           API) and forces the portable implementations with
                           -DBR_AES_X86NI=0 -DBR_SSE2=0 -DBR_RDRAND=0, since
                           the kernel does not enable SSE in CR0/CR4 or save
                           XMM state across context switches.

  compat/string.h          declares the few libc routines BearSSL includes
                           <string.h> for; they are implemented in
                           src/kstring.c.

  src/bearssl_glue.c       supplies br_prng_seeder_system() and time(), the
                           two host-environment symbols left dangling by the
                           exclusions above. Neither is called on any live
                           path.

  src/tls.c                the client itself: entropy seeding, the transport
                           callbacks onto hawkOS's TCP, and a permissive
                           X.509 engine. Read the security note at the top
                           of that file before trusting this with anything.

Only src/ and inc/ are needed to build. The rest of the upstream tree (its
own Makefile, test suite, samples and the T0 compiler) is kept for reference
but is not used by hawkOS.
